q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT JOIN EMPLOYEE USING (EMPLOYEE_ID) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT JOIN EMPLOYEE USING (EMPLOYEE_ID) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries join the PROJECT and EMPLOYEE tables on EMPLOYEE_ID, compute the average of EXPERIENCE_YEARS grouped by PROJECT_ID, and round the result to 2 decimal places. The only minor syntactic differences are in the column aliases and the use of GROUP BY 1 in Q2, which refers to the first column in the SELECT list (PROJECT_ID).
